china_race_dynamics.text: We keep hearing about this race, this race against China. … Well, we don’t control the entity that we’re trying to create, and neither does China.

deepseek.reason: The speaker dismisses the 'race against China' framing by noting that neither the US nor China controls the entity being created.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The quote clearly questions the race framing, though it does not use explicit policy language.

china_race_dynamics.text: China has adopted an AI system that is total surveillance of their entire population there. It is non-democratic. It is quite oppressive. Their goal is to be able to surveil every single member of their society, know what they are doing, know what they are purchasing, and for oppressive reasons so that no one gets out of line. Can you talk about the need to, when we adopt, when we approve AI and choose the architecture for our AI, how important it is to make sure that transparency, that respecting privacy, independence, how important it is to have those elements of democracy itself ingrained and embodied in our AI models?
china_race_dynamics.context: Verbatim congressional hearing on the federal government in the age of artificial intelligence, with a representative questioning an expert witness.

deepseek.reason: The speaker criticizes China's surveillance AI but does not discuss making AI competition with China a policy priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: China is discussed as an oppressive surveillance example, not in terms of race dynamics.

china_race_dynamics.text: As reported by the United States intelligence community in its Worldwide Threat Assessment recently, Russia, China, North Korea, and other state actors are continuing to conduct malign influence operations aimed at disseminating disinformation and magnifying U.S. societal divisions and interfering with the upcoming U.S. elections. [...] the introduction of generative AI sort of amplifies the possibilities of this exacerbated threat. [...] Dr. Turner Lee, what effect can we expect AI-generated deepfakes and misinformation to have on Americans' trust, their trust in the election process?
china_race_dynamics.context: House committee hearing on AI oversight, March 21, 2024, with Mr. Lynch questioning witnesses about AI-enabled election interference.

deepseek.reason: The speaker mentions China only as a source of election disinformation, not as an AI competition priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement does not address the China AI race framing or any listed tradeoff.

china_race_dynamics.text: I just see us in a competition, you know, and I know China right now has full spectrum surveillance of its entire population. [...] The other aspect of this that I worry about is the power of AI [...] Mr. Timmons talked about the weaponization of weapon systems that would be completely autonomous [...] how can we, in the United States, in developing our AI policy, influence other countries, even in Europe, friendly, you know, and allies, other democracies, how do we make that happen?
china_race_dynamics.context: Congressional hearing or briefing on White House AI policy, December 6, 2023.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says he sees the US in a competition with China and asks how US AI policy can influence allies.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The competition framing is explicit, though the ally-influence question is not a separate tradeoff.

china_race_dynamics.text: This Executive Order directs the Treasury to draft regulations that require disclosure of or prohibit certain outbound foreign investments into mainland China, to Hong Kong, or to Macau. [...] it only covers certain aspects of advanced computing, quantum information technologies, and AI, and that other activity, including financial investment, might not be covered. [...] if there are any gaps that you recognize that might be covered, just to give Congress an idea of what direction we might be looking at.
china_race_dynamics.context: Congressional hearing on CFIUS and national security, where Rep. Lynch questions a witness about the scope of outbound investment restrictions on China.

china_race_dynamics.text: We are in a competition here, right. We are in a competition. We do not want to cede this space to China. How do we keep up with them or, you know, maintain a lead in this area and ethically do due diligence in terms of our obligation to protect privacy rights and, you know, democratic ideals?
china_race_dynamics.context: House Oversight Committee hearing on using cutting-edge technologies to keep America safe, where Rep. Lynch questions panelists about the AI competition with China and Russia.

deepseek.reason: The speaker explicitly says the US is in a competition with China and asks how to maintain a lead while doing ethical due diligence.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement directly endorses competition and adds a clear ethical-safeguard condition.
